record.title: Reboot acceptance extends beyond the printed message
record.method: Explicit UART request; observed recovery return; full data-volume check
record.observation: The corrected UART listener survived input, accepted the explicit request and returned through BSD shutdown to recovery. A later remote-only run passed the former three-minute cutoff, rebooted on request and passed full data fsck with an unchanged root.
record.limits: The command is a dedicated reboot channel, not a shell. It depends on a live polling path and does not guarantee recovery from arbitrary kernel failure.

exhibits.title: A board mismatch at the same MMIO offset
rows: Not handled as the native UART source
exhibits.interpretation: A plausible driver name does not make the register layouts compatible. The first receive event exposed that mismatch.

exhibits.title: Progress beyond the printed acknowledgement
rows: Harmless RX survived; recovery about 6 s after request
Ten heartbeats past old cutoff; recovery about 6 s later
512 MiB; fsck exit 0; clean bit set
exhibits.interpretation: The record distinguishes the first interrupt-masking correction from the later explicit IER clear. Actual recovery and filesystem checks complete the reboot claim.

excerpts.content:
The phone Apple tree originally exposed `uart0` at the real A64 UART0 MMIO
address `0x01c28000` as `uart,s5l8900x`. AppleS5L8900XSerial attached in the
first physical UART-command trial. Its Samsung UCON register at offset 4
overlaps A64 UART IER. The first trial stopped printing after host RX and did
not reach either command acknowledgement or the five-minute fallback. The
live A64 UART0 interrupt is GIC SPI 32.

[…]

The corrected five-minute physical gate captured
`spi32_before=00000001 after=00000000 ier=00000001`: masking was actually
needed on the phone. A harmless RX byte did not stop the idle or UART
heartbeats. The full token was accepted, `MACH Reboot` appeared, and
Jumpdrive returned six seconds after the host request. The subsequent full
512 MiB data copy had its HFS clean bit set and passed `fsck_hfs -dfn` with
exit 0; the root partition SHA-256 remained
`a2a4776df7602d41cd6e83e7b873ae4cfc0db30cff87303b6d608e520c01e17c`.
UART0 IER still read 1 in that gate because U-Boot had left it enabled.

[…]

Its first phone
run logged `spi32_before=00000001 after=00000000 ier=00000000` at listener
startup. Ten subsequent UART heartbeats retained `ier=00000000 spi32=0
remask=0` beyond the old three-minute cutoff. The host requested a reboot,
and Jumpdrive returned about six seconds later. Its complete post-run data
copy had the clean bit set and passed fsck with exit 0; the root hash was
unchanged.
excerpts.note: Exact selected notebook passages. Ellipses mark omitted material; source line numbers refer to the reviewed document.
